description: issue #677 (SP5) + issue #847 + issue #738: `clear_screen` clears the one shared drawing surface exactly once (not once per addressed turtle), and homes every addressed turtle — here just :a, so this is the case where the pre-#738 "home the current turtle" behaviour and the ruled "home every addressed turtle" behaviour agree, which makes it the regression guard for that change. The homing is **observable** — `move`/`turn` for the homing, with NO `draw-segment` even though the pen is down, because the same instruction goes on to clear the drawing (spec/rendering.md:36 describes what a pen-down move contributes to the RETAINED SCENE, and :150's "Clear operations" row fixes `clear_screen`'s contribution at *cleared*; escalated to the maintainer as issue #858). Under `tell [ :a ]` the homing pair carries the homed turtle's `turtle_id` (1) so a per-turtle state reducer homes exactly :a — the turtle the runtime actually homed — not the main turtle. The `clear` carries no `turtle_id` even though exactly one turtle is addressed: spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:113 makes that unconditional — "A `clear` event describes the shared surface rather than any turtle, so it is not turtle-specific and carries no turtle identity" — and consumers "MUST NOT read a `clear` event as an instruction to move a turtle", so the identity lives on the movement events alone. Every change of the addressed set — here from `tell` — also emits the addressing `primitive` event carrying `addressing: { addressed_turtle_ids, current_turtle_id }`, so a consumer can identify the addressed turtle set (issue #766, spec/rendering.md:193); `ask`/`each` emit one again when the previous set is restored, on every exit path.
